svg.text: Risk A2, resolved — a bound copy, refreshed after every command
A slide object that copies a placeholder keeps real coordinates, marked bound. The layout is the truth; the copies are repaired after every command, never refused.
Two separate fields: purpose is what people see and name; bound_to_placeholder is technical and only says which placeholder to copy.
x, y, w, h: the frame
· user-facing: shown in the UI, unique in the
layout, matched when a slide changes layout
x, y, w, h, object style: copies
· technical: the id of the placeholder; frame and
object style read-only while set; no purpose here
never the frame or object style of a bound object
the frame and object-style copies, nothing else

A purpose is looked up through the placeholder, so renaming it in the layout renames it everywhere; a slide object never stores one. Other layout objects (a logo) are not copied: they are drawn from the layout and can be selected on a slide.
2 The same update and undo, now with one real step each
One step: the placeholder moves. It does not list followers.
Copies are refreshed from the layout. Change events go out.
The placeholder moves back; settle refreshes the copies.
A placeholder is moved or resized
→ its frame is copied into every object bound to it
A colleague adds a bound object while I update the layout
→ it gets the current frame in the same repair; nothing was missed because no follower list was carried
Undo brings back an object with an old frame
→ objects bound to it lose bound_to_placeholder and stay where they are, as free boxes (empty ones go in the command itself)
→ SetSlideLayout carries the new binding: same purpose, so the new placeholder’s id; otherwise cleared. settle heals anything left over the same way
Free box from a bound object
→ drop bound_to_placeholder; the copy already is its frame, so nothing is computed
4 To confirm before building (first TDD step)
and emit ObjectsChanged for them. Not yet checked; the hook is documented as “recalculate here”.
the copies are a pure function of layouts, slide pointers and bindings, so every server and a replay from the log get the same ones.
if it only applies server events, the repair’s events are all it needs; if it applies commands itself, it needs the same repair.
the repair visits only the layouts and slides the command touched, not the whole deck.
between steps a copy may lag; code there calls model.frame_of(obj), which reads the layout.
